question: In the morning, a warehouse had 153 boxes. By midday, they received 7 times as many. In the afternoon, the count increased 6 times. By evening, it increased 6 times again. That night, 20 more boxes arrived. The next morning, 70 more boxes were added. How many boxes are in the warehouse?

Emma started her business with 117 customers. In the first week, she gained 4 customers. In the second week, she lost 27 customers. In the third week, she gained 13 customers. In the fourth week, she lost 28 customers. In the fifth week, she gained 11 customers. A competitor had 100 customers. How many customers does Emma have at the end?

A restaurant started with 71 meals to prepare. Production doubled during the rush hour. Then, 37 meals were canceled. Orders multiplied 9 times due to a promotion. Her friend's restaurant had 200 meals. Finally, they were divided equally among 5 kitchen stations. How many meals does each station handle?

In the morning, a store had 102 items. By midday, inventory tripled. In the afternoon, it multiplied 7 times. By evening, 61 items were received. That night, 895 items were sold. The next day, 80 items were added. Finally, 1251 items were removed. A nearby store had 500 items. How many items does the store have?

Alex started with 197 dollars. He spent 185 dollars. His remaining money multiplied 4 times. He earned 71 dollars. He earned 58 more dollars. His total increased 7 times. He then spent 752 dollars. His friend Ben had 400 dollars. How much money does Alex have?

In the morning, a warehouse had 218 boxes. By midday, half of the boxes were moved to another location. In the afternoon, 40 boxes were shipped out. By evening, 55 boxes arrived. That night, 4 more boxes were received. The next morning, 51 boxes were sent out. Converting to pallets (1 pallet = 2 boxes), how many boxes remain?

A shop started with 151 items. They received 25 more items. Their inventory increased 6 times. They got 7 more items. Finally, they added 47 more items. Her father had 80 items. How many items does the shop have at the end?

A company started with 169 units of product. The inventory multiplied 4 times. Then it was divided back by 4. They removed 91 units due to damage. The remaining was reduced to a third. They then lost 20 units. Finally, they added 77 units. Converting to hundreds, how many units are in stock?

A project started with 35 tasks. It multiplied 7 times in scope. The total doubled. They removed 425 tasks as duplicates. They added 79 new tasks. Finally, they added a dozen more tasks. How many total tasks remain? Converting to work days (assume 12 tasks per day), how many days of work?

In the morning, a warehouse had 97 boxes. By midday, they received 54 boxes. In the afternoon, 17 more boxes arrived. By evening, 72 boxes were added. The next day, the count increased 4 times. It increased 4 times again. Finally, 24 more boxes were added. A neighboring warehouse had 50 boxes. How many boxes does the warehouse have?

In the morning, a factory had 105 units. They multiplied production 8 times. The output was then divided by 5. They removed 166 units for quality control. Finally, 1 more unit was removed. How many units remain?

A business started with 27 items. They multiplied their stock 4 times. They added 21 items. They removed 75 items to clear space. Their inventory then increased 6 times. Finally, it increased 8 times. They added 15 more items. Converting to cases (assume 1 case = 10 items), how many items are there?
A bookshop started with 45 books. They added 31 books. They removed 23 books for repair. They removed 16 more books. Finally, 6 more books were removed. How many books remain on the shelves?

A gallery had 144 artworks. They added 23 artworks. They removed 17 artworks for restoration. They removed another 139 artworks. Their collection increased 4 times. Then it increased 9 times. A competing gallery had 100 artworks. How many artworks does this gallery have?

A factory started with 236 units. In the morning, production tripled. By midday, they added 58 units. In the afternoon, they added 17 units. By evening, 268 units were removed. Finally, 276 units were removed. How many units remain?

A business started with 59 items. They doubled their stock in the morning. By midday, 67 items were removed. By afternoon, 11 more items were removed. By evening, their inventory tripled. Finally, it doubled. How many items does the business have?

A trader started with 150 items. They gained 5 items. They gained 9 more items. They lost 152 items. They gained 49 items. They lost 53 items. Their partner had 100 items. How many items does the trader have?

A business started with 206 items. They removed 75 items to a branch. They received 33 items. They tripled their remaining stock. They got 27 more items. Finally, they got 79 more items. How many items do they have at the end?

A company started with 66 units. They added 43 units. They removed 55 units. They doubled their remaining inventory. They increased it 5 times. They then divided it equally among 4 teams. Finally, each team received 68 additional units. Her friend's company had 500 units. A third company had 600 units. How many units does the first company have?

A warehouse started with 185 boxes. They removed 140 boxes. They removed 22 more boxes. They removed another 22 boxes. Their remaining inventory increased 4 times. A competing warehouse had 400 boxes. How many boxes does this warehouse have?

A shop started with 65 items. They tripled their inventory in the morning. By midday, 153 items were sold. By afternoon, 2 more items were sold. By evening, they increased their inventory 4 times. How many items does the shop have at the end?

In the morning, a factory had 27 units. Production increased 6 times by midday. By afternoon, 17 units were added. By evening, 36 units were added. A competitor produced 80 units. Their output then increased 5 times. How many units were produced?
A company started with 74 units. They added 21 units. They added 64 units. They added 17 units. They removed 105 units. They added 65 units. How many units do they have?

In the morning, a business had 229 units. By afternoon, production increased 9 times. By evening, it increased 6 times. It increased another 2 times. It increased yet again by 2 times. Due to losses, 45695 units were removed. Converting to thousands, how many units remain? How many days would it take (assume 5000 units per day)?

A business started with 97 items. They removed 3 items. They removed 10 items. Their stock increased 6 times. It increased 3 times again. They added 23 items. Finally, they added 31 items. Their competitor had 200 items. How many items do they have?
